page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.large is a burstable, entry-level virtual server belonging to the shared t5 family. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture, it utilizes an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz with L1 data, L2, and L3 cache sizes of 32 KB, 1.0 MB, and 33 MB respectively. The instance provides 2 vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core via hyperthreading, paired with 2.0 GB of total RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units, local instance storage, or baseline network bandwidth, requiring external disk volumes for persistent storage operations.

Empirical benchmark results indicate baseline performance typical of burstable resource tiers. In synthetic CPU workloads, the instance recorded a single-core stress-ng score of 1078.28 and a multi-core result of 2088.79, falling into the bottom quartiles. PassMark testing yielded an overall CPU score of 2509.4 and an encryption score of 795.78, accompanied by an extended instructions score of 2375.51 supported by AVX-512 extensions. Memory throughput reached 15.52 GB/s for uncached large-block reads and 13.96 GB/s for writes. Application benchmarks demonstrated 2.37 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 1.54 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Because of its shared-core architecture and fractional compute model, the ecs.t5-c1m1.large prioritizes budget efficiency over sustained throughput. The primary operational tradeoff involves CPU throttling when baseline credits are exhausted under sustained load, as well as the tight 2.0 GB memory envelope which restricts multi-threaded execution and large in-memory datasets. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for low-traffic web servers, light automation scripts, periodic cron jobs, small database mirrors, and non-production testing environments where compute demands remain intermittent.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.large is an entry-tier, shared-core burstable instance tailored for light, intermittent workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers two virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 2.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 1.0 GB per vCPU, without bundled local storage or baseline network bandwidth guarantees, relying instead on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations place this configuration in the lower performance brackets, with a PassMark CPU score of 2509.4 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 2088.79, reflecting its burstable execution model and constrained CPU quota. Its memory subsystem achieves 15.52 GB/s in large-block read operations. With low resource allocation and lack of dedicated compute, this instance offers a cost-effective platform for development staging, lightweight batch processing, basic web serving, and low-traffic background jobs.
